title: Mike K NDE 4356
content: In early 1969 I had an out of body experience. At least this is what I think; it is hard to tell. I was on the Aircraft Carrier USS Hancock during a recovery. I was on the flight deck to de-arm the ordinance of one of our planes when it landed during night flight ops. An F-8 crashed on the fantail (round down) exploding on impact. The airplane broke in half; the cockpit with the pilot went forward off the ship. The debris came flying at us at 110 mph the burning fuel following. I have lived that moment a million times. After all these years, I can still see the nose of the plane rise up at an awkward angle. At that point, I got a sick feeling. I knew this was going to be bad. The sound was unreal as the fuel burst and ignited. I was staring at a wall of burning jet fuel coming right at me. It was all in slow motion almost frame by frame. I find this hard to put on paper. I felt myself looking at myself I was high and to the right of where I was standing. Then the word 'move' came to me loud, very loud and clear. I moved and so did the guy next to me. After the initial blast, I got up and manned a fire hose. Thirty years later, I found that guy on a website and e-mailed him. He said he pulled me from the fire. I don't remember that. It all happened very fast as you could imagine. I remember seeing the ship from high up at least a hundred feet or more as the ship seemed small. I remember feeling as if I really didn't want to go back. The voice I heard left no doubt that I was to go back.

out_of_body.vantage_other_detail: High and to the right of where he was standing; later 'high up at least a hundred feet or more' seeing the ship seem small.

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Explosion/crash of an F-8 aircraft on the USS Hancock flight deck during night operations.

stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: Experience centers on an out-of-body vantage during an explosion, with an auditory command ('move') and later a sense of being required to return; no tunnel/otherworldly realm described.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Auditory command ('move') during OBE in a real-world emergency; later confirmation from another crewman that he was pulled from the fire, which he does not remember.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “Then the word 'move' came to me loud, very loud and clear.” / “I remember seeing the ship from high up at least a hundred feet or more as the ship seemed small.” / “I remember feeling as if I really didn't want to go back. The voice I heard left no doubt that I was to go back.”
